title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G = GL(2)_S over a base scheme S, PG = PGL(2)_S. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', i.e. the study of braid/loop-type relations realised by sections of PGL(2). On the previous page he defined Δ(ρ) = Tr²ρ / det ρ for a section ρ of G (formula 19). Δ is invariant under the homotheties ρ ↦ λρ, λ ∈ Γ(G_m), and under conjugation.

On this page:
- Δ descends to a morphism (20) PG → E¹, presumably the affine line. It is given by Δ(ρ̃) = Δ(ρ) = (Tr ρ)²/det ρ and is invariant under inner automorphisms. So it is the natural invariant function on PGL₂, the analogue of the characteristic-polynomial map.

Proposition. Let ρ̃, ρ̃' be sections of PG, with ρ̃ regular (non-scalar in every fibre) and Tr ρ invertible. Then ρ̃ and ρ̃' are locally conjugate over S if and only if ρ̃' is regular and Δ(ρ̃) = Δ(ρ̃') (21).
- Necessity is clear from (17)–(18): ρ' = λuρu⁻¹ gives Tr ρ' = λ Tr ρ and det ρ' = λ² det ρ.
- Sufficiency (assuming Δ, equivalently Tr ρ, invertible):
  1. Locally on S choose λ with λ² = det ρ'/det ρ. Replacing ρ by λρ, we may assume det ρ = det ρ'.
  2. Then (18) becomes (22): Tr²ρ' = Tr²ρ.
  3. Since τ = Tr ρ is invertible, ε = τ'/τ satisfies ε² = 1, so ε ∈ Γ(μ₂) and Tr ρ' = Tr(ερ). Also det(ερ) = ε² det ρ = det ρ'.
  4. So ρ' and ερ are regular with the same characteristic polynomial, hence locally conjugate in GL₂. This gives local conjugacy of ρ̃' and ρ̃ in PG.

The next page gives counterexamples when Tr is not invertible and the base is non-reduced. It then turns to the relative position of two sections ρ, σ, via ε₀ = σ⁻¹ρ and ε₁ = ρσ⁻¹ being unipotent. This is the set-up for braid-type relations in PGL₂.
errors: Step 1 extracts a square root λ² = det ρ'/det ρ 'loc. sur S'. This is only étale-local (fppf-local in characteristic 2), not Zariski-local, so 'locally conjugate' must be understood in the fppf/étale topology. Likewise μ₂ is not étale in characteristic 2. Grothendieck does not specify the topology.
The step 'same trace and det plus regular ⇒ locally conjugate' is used without proof. It is standard: locally a cyclic vector exists, giving a companion matrix, but it is a tacit step.

The proposition as stated is muddled in the manuscript (crossed-out words). The intended hypothesis 'Tr ρ invertible' is added only afterwards as the condition under which the conditions are sufficient.

ideas.what: The invariant Δ = Tr²/det : PGL₂ → A¹, conjugation-invariant, as the quotient map for conjugacy classes in PGL₂
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint quotient / Chevalley–Steinberg map for PGL₂ (PGL₂ // PGL₂ ≅ A¹)
ideas.where_published: related material in SGA 3 (regular elements, Exp. XIII–XIV)

ideas.what: Regular sections of PGL₂ over a base with invertible Δ are locally conjugate iff they have the same Δ; this fails over non-reduced bases when Tr is not invertible
ideas.modern_name: Local conjugacy of regular elements with the same characteristic polynomial over a base scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Steinberg / Kostant for regular elements; SGA 3 for group schemes
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 treats regular elements of reductive group schemes

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct (modulo the choice of topology) lemma on conjugacy of regular elements of PGL₂ over a base, preparatory to the braid/lacets study. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'loc. sur 𝒯' should read 'loc. sur S'.
'qui prise ... quotient en' is likely 'qui passe au quotient en'.
E' in (20) is likely E¹ (Grothendieck's notation for the affine line).
'invariants par automorphismes [?] int.' = 'invariant par automorphismes intérieurs'.
'Ces conditions sont suffisantes [-quand-] Δ(ρ̃) inv.' : the struck word is 'quand'. The sense is 'sufficient when Δ(ρ̃) is invertible, i.e. Tr ρ invertible'.
